extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining and processing reissue patent applications, including handling of reissue oaths/declarations, supplemental oaths, amendments (pre- and post-allowance), interferences, divisional/continuation reissue practice, and application of applicable CFR and statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective initial reissue oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.175(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reissue oath/declaration fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.175(a), the examiner will notify applicant in an Office action, rejecting the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reply to the Office action, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration should be submitted dealing with the noted defects. If the initial oath/declaration (1) failed to provide any error statement, or (2) attempted to provide one but failed to identify any error under 35 U.S.C. 251, the examiner should reject all claims as being based upon a defective reissue oath/declaration and point out the failure to comply with 37 CFR 1.175. A supplemental oath/declaration stating an error under 35 U.S.C. 251 must be submitted to support the reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath required when prior-identified errors no longer relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: If the initial reissue oath/declaration properly identified errors but, due to changes/amendments during prosecution, none of those identified errors are relied upon any more, a supplemental oath/declaration is needed to identify at least one error now relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental oath need not state that prior-identified errors are no longer being corrected. Because a proper statement of error was provided initially, applicant may, at applicant's option, defer submission of the supplemental oath/declaration until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance by requesting such deferral (this request will be considered a complete reply to the rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: When cumulative supplemental reissue oath advisable (practical suggestion)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is suggested that the reissue applicant wait until the case is in condition for allowance, then submit a cumulative supplemental reissue oath/declaration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental oath/declaration need not be submitted with each amendment or additional correction; cumulative submission is permitted and suggested to avoid repeated filings during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory conditions triggering 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) supplemental oath
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) must be submitted before allowance and will be required where: (A) the application is otherwise in condition for allowance; (B) amendments or other corrections of errors in the patent were made subsequent to the last oath/declaration filed; and (C) at least one of those amendments or corrections corrects an error under 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental oath may be submitted with any reply prior to allowance and may be submitted to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251 where indicated that it will overcome the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner encouragement to request supplemental oath by phone; final action if not supplied
rubrics_metrics.description: When a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) is required, the examiner is encouraged to telephone applicant and request the submission by fax; if circumstances do not permit or applicant declines/unable, the examiner should issue a final Office action (final rejection) and use form paragraph 14.05.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of telephone/fax is encouraged to expedite compliance; absent prompt submission, formal rejection procedure is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 14.05.02 use and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 14.05.02 notifies applicant of requirement for supplemental reissue oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) before allowance and rejects the claims as defective until the supplemental oath/declaration is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sample acceptable language for the supplemental oath: e.g., 'Every error in the patent which was corrected in the present reissue application, and is not covered by a prior oath/declaration submitted in this application, arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant.' Examiner notes specify bracket insertions (claims list; oath/declaration), and when not to use this paragraph: do not use if no amendments were made since last oath; cannot be used in Ex parte Quayle action; do not use in examiner's amendment; the supplemental oath must be filed prior to Notice of Allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance correction amendments governed by 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections of patent errors after allowance must be submitted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the notice of allowance. An amendment filed before payment of the issue fee may be entered on the recommendation of the primary examiner and approval of the supervisory examiner without withdrawing the case from issue. An amendment filed after payment of the issue fee must be accompanied by a petition including the fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) and a showing of good and sufficient reasons, decided by the Group Director. Because such amendments affect disclosure or claim scope, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier. A supplemental reissue oath/declaration must accompany the amendment and must state that the errors arose without deceptive intention; it need only be directed to the errors being corrected after allowance and need not cover earlier errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections that are not physical amendments (e.g., filing certified foreign priority) still governed by amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An error to be corrected after allowance that does not include an amendment of the specification or claims (for example, filing a certified copy of the original foreign application to obtain priority) still must comply with 37 CFR 1.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where no amendment is physically entered, the correction of the patent is an amendment and the same procedural requirements apply for supplemental oath/declaration and petitions when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application examined same as original (37 CFR 1.176)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application, including all its claims, is subject to be examined in the same manner as original applications; claims are subject to any and all rejections the examiner deems appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It does not matter whether claims are identical to those of the patent or changed; prior prosecution history does not prevent rejections in the reissue application. Claims in a reissue application enjoy no 'presumption of validity.' Previously considered or unconsidered prior art may be used during reissue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud/inequitable conduct/duty of disclosure policy in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office no longer investigates and rejects reissue applications under 37 CFR 1.56; the Office will not comment upon duty of disclosure issues in reissue applications except to note they are no longer considered during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's statement in the reissue oath/declaration of lack of deceptive intent will be accepted as dispositive except in special circumstances such as an admission or judicial determination of fraud, inequitable conduct, or violation of the duty of disclosure. In such special circumstances, after consulting with the Group Special Program Examiner, a rejection should be made using form paragraphs 14.21.09 or 14.22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of admissions or judicial determinations as exception to accepting lack of deceptive intent
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission or judicial determination of fraud, inequitable conduct, or violation of duty of disclosure is a special circumstance that justifies not accepting applicant's statement of lack of deceptive intent as dispositive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any admission must be explicit, unequivocal, and not subject to other interpretation. If a rejection is made based on such an admission and applicant offers any reasonable interpretation of the facts that would not lead to a conclusion of fraud/inequitable conduct, the rejection should be withdrawn. External information believed to be an admission should never be used by the examiner nor made of record in the application without proper basis; consult SPE/SPLO and use form paragraphs where appropriate. Form paragraph 14.21.09 is for judicial determinations known externally; form paragraph 14.22 is for admissions or evidence in the application record (use bracket guidance per MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral when protest filed in reissue where patent is in interference
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protest is filed in a reissue application related to a patent involved in a pending interference proceeding, the reissue application should be referred to the Special Program Law Office (SPLO) before acting on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPLO will check that (A) all parties to the interference are aware of the filing of the reissue and (B) the Office does not allow claims in the reissue which are unpatentable over the pending interference count(s), or found unpatentable in the interference proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent reissue and reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.565(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and a reexamination proceeding (with order pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525) are pending concurrently on a patent, a decision will normally be made to merge the two proceedings or to stay one of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner becomes aware of concurrent reissue and reexamination, inform the Group Special Program Examiner immediately. When an order granting reexamination has been issued, forward files to the Office of the Deputy Assistant Commissioner for Patent Policy and Projects for decision whether to merge or stay. If the original patent is involved in an interference, consult the administrative patent judge before taking action; do not grant reissue without judge's approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reissue to provoke an interference (limits and requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application may be placed into interference, and a patentee may provoke an interference by filing a reissue application that (A) adds copied claims not present in the original patent, (B) amends claims to correspond to another patent/application, or (C) contains at least one error (not directed to provoking interference) appropriate for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue error must be based upon applicant error; cannot be based solely on Office error for failing to declare an interference. When copying/amending claims to provoke an interference, the reissue oath/declaration must assert applicant erred in failing to include claims of the proper scope in the original application. The copied/amended claims' subject matter must be supported by the original patent disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. A reissue applicant cannot present added/amended claims to provoke an interference if the claims were deliberately omitted from the patent (e.g., described as undesirable). The issue date of the patent with which interference is sought must be less than 1 year prior to presentation of the copied/amended claims (35 U.S.C. 135(b)). If the reissue includes broadened claims, the reissue must be filed within two years from issue date of the original patent (35 U.S.C. 251 and MPEP § 1412.03). If a reissue is filed while the patent is in interference, notify the Board within 10 days (37 CFR 1.660(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction and election of species in reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not require restriction in a reissue application (37 CFR 1.176 and MPEP § 1440); restriction may only be requested by applicant (37 CFR 1.177 and MPEP § 1451).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where the original patent contains claims to different inventions considered independent and distinct, the examiner should not require restriction in the reissue. If the reissue presents claims for the first time that are distinct and separate from those of the patent, follow In re Amos practice (MPEP § 1412.01). Failure to timely file a divisional application is not considered error correctable by reissue. If the original specification shows intent not to claim the invention, that invention cannot be added by reissue; added claims may be rejected for lack of defect in the original patent and lack of error in obtaining the original patent. When the original patent contains claims to multiple species and the reissue contains the same species, election of species should not be required even if no allowable generic claim exists; if reissue presents species not claimed in the original, election of species is still not required, but added claims may be rejected for lack of defect/lack of error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional reissue applications practice (37 CFR 1.177)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may issue several reissued patents for distinct and separate parts of the thing patented upon applicant demand and payment of required fees; 37 CFR 1.177 governs reissue in divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When divisional reissue applications are filed, appropriate amendments to continuing data entries must be made so adequate notice is provided that more than one reissue application has been filed for a single original patent. Office policy routinely waives simultaneous issuance requirement (37 CFR 1.177) sua sponte under 37 CFR 1.183 prior to examination via letter from Special Program Law Office; examiners should check for such a 1.177 letter in each divisional file and forward to SPLO if absent. Questions on propriety of divisional reissue and continuation reissue applications should be referred via SPE to SPLO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation reissue applications practice (In re Graff guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation of a reissue (continuation reissue) is permitted where it complies with reissue rules; parent and continuation should be examined together if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend continuing data entries to identify parent-continuation relationship and provide notice. If parent issues prior to continuation examination, carefully review continuation claims for double patenting over the parent; where examined together, make provisional double patenting rejection in both cases for overlapping claims (see MPEP § 804). Terminal disclaimers filed to obviate obviousness-type double patenting ensure common ownership for the unexpired term. If the parent reissue issues without cross-reference to the continuation, require the continuation (or parent) be amended by Certificate of Correction to include cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to reissue specification (37 CFR 1.121(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification, other than the claims, must be made by submission of the entire text of newly added or rewritten paragraph(s) with markings (underlining for additions, brackets for deletions) and must indicate the precise point where the paragraph is located; an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of its text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent (not prior amendments). Added paragraphs must be submitted completely underlined. Changes are handled as blocked paragraph insertions (assigned letter/number) with a caret indicating incorporation point, so applicants need not be concerned with page formatting. This section does not apply to claims or drawings amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to reissue claims (37 CFR 1.121(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to claims must present the entire text of each claim being amended and of each claim added, with markings; patent claims must not be renumbered and numbering of added claims must follow the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use underlining for added subject matter and brackets for deleted subject matter. If a claim is amended, include a parenthetical such as '(amended)' or '(twice amended)' after the original claim number. Each amendment submission must set forth the status (pending or cancelled) as of the amendment date of all patent claims and added claims. Each amendment when originally submitted must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure for the amendment and any additional comments on separate pages from the amendment text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendments in reissue (37 CFR 1.121(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the original patent drawings are not permitted directly; changes must be by filing a new sheet of drawings with amended figures identified as 'amended' and added figures identified as 'new'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a change is desired, file a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval; the sketch should be on a separate paper. Follow 37 CFR 1.84 for drawing format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure correspondence and prohibition on new matter or enlargement beyond two years
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended when required to correct inaccuracies and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings. No reissue patent shall be granted enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from grant of the original patent. No amendment may introduce new matter or be made in an expired patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification, including claims and drawings, which is in effect as of the filing date of the reissue application. These provisions apply to amendments submitted on or after December 1, 1997; earlier amendments need not be re-submitted but will be entered if re-submitted unless directed otherwise by the SPE or SPRE.
